Yes, it is possible to start tomato seeds in bunches or clusters. Here are some tips for starting tomato seeds in bunches:

1. Seed starting containers: Use seed trays, pots, or containers that are large enough to accommodate multiple tomato seedlings growing together. Cells or modules that are at least 3-4 inches wide work well.

2. Sow seeds: Place 2-4 tomato seeds together in each cell or container. Space the seeds a couple inches apart within the container.

3. Soil mix: Use a quality seed starting mix or potting soil. Ensure the soil is loose and well-draining.

4. Depth: Plant the tomato seeds about 1/4 to 1/2 inch deep in the soil.

5. Germination: Keep the soil consistently moist but not waterlogged. Tomato seeds typically germinate in 5-12 days.

6. Thinning: Once the seedlings emerge, allow them to grow for a week or two. Then, gently thin out the weaker or smaller seedlings, leaving the 1-2 strongest ones per cluster.

7. Transplanting: When the seedlings have their first set of true leaves, transplant the clusters into larger pots or outdoors, taking care not to disturb the roots of the remaining plants.

Starting tomato seeds in bunches can be a space-saving technique, but make sure to thin and transplant the seedlings properly to avoid overcrowding as they grow.
